reasons: Covers refusal, naming, location and fixture presence with direct checks.
Refusal tests check the error type and message, so a silent pass is unlikely.

terms.meaning: A fixed set of test data that tests depend on and expect to stay unchanged.
A check placed in front of an action that refuses it when the action would be unsafe.
A cleaned-up version of a name that is safe to use as a single folder name.
Running the pipeline on saved outputs rather than a live model.

used_by: Run by pytest. No importing file is visible.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and why the fixture is read-only
sections.what: Brings in the recording helpers and the test runner. The module docstring explains why the saved fixture must not be overwritten by a live run.
sections.why: The docstring states that an overwrite would move the baseline with nothing signalling the change.

sections.name: TestALiveRunCannotWriteIntoTheFixture
sections.title: Live runs cannot write the fixture
sections.what: Checks the write guard refuses the fixture root, any folder inside it, and a path that climbs back in with dot-dot. It also checks that replays may read the fixture and that the live folder may be written.
sections.why: The docstring says the path is resolved before the check, because a check on the raw text would be fooled by a path such as one that climbs back in.
sections.watch_out: A new way of writing a path that resolution does not normalise would need its own test.

sections.name: TestTheSinkIsNamespacedByProviderAndModel
sections.title: Each provider and model has its own folder
sections.what: Checks that a save location includes both provider and model, that two models or two providers get different folders, that no save location lands in the fixture, that a replay is refused a save location, and that an empty case id is refused.
sections.why: The docstring says a shared folder would let a second run silently replace the first, the same kind of defect the guard exists to stop.
sections.watch_out: The provider and model names used are examples. A new naming scheme needs its own checks.

sections.name: TestSlugging
sections.title: Names become safe folder names
sections.what: Checks that provider and model names are flattened into one safe folder segment, with slashes and dot-dot removed, and that a name that would become empty is refused.
sections.why: Likely reason: model names contain slashes and spaces that could otherwise create nested folders or folders that escape the save area.
sections.watch_out: The list of example names is the only specification here, so new naming rules need new examples.

sections.name: TestTheFixtureIsWhereTheTestsThinkItIs
sections.title: Fixture folder is where tests expect
sections.what: Checks the fixture folder exists with the expected case and portfolio folders, that the live folder is separate from it, and that no folder named for a live provider has been placed inside the fixture.
sections.why: The docstring says that if the fixture moved, the guard would protect an empty folder while every other test passed.
sections.watch_out: Fails if someone adds a folder named together, openai, deepseek or live to the fixture, even on purpose.

summary: Checks that a live model run can never write into the synthetic recordings fixture and that each provider and model saves to its own separate folder.
purpose: Protects the reproducibility baseline. The synthetic recordings are the saved outputs that tests are pinned to, and a live run overwriting them would change the baseline without any test failing.
why: The module docstring explains the risk: replay would still match itself, but to a different answer, and the mutation tests would be tied to whatever a provider returned that day.
how: The file tests the write guard with paths inside, at, and climbing back into the fixture folder. It tests that save folders are named by provider and model, that names are flattened into safe single folder names, and that the fixture folder exists and holds no live provider folders.
inputs: Paths and provider and model names passed to the recording helpers. Nothing is sent over the network.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest.
risks: These tests check the path guard and naming only. A bug in code that never calls the guard would not be caught here.
debug: If a test fails, open packages/orchestration/recordings.py and check guard_write, recording_sink and slug. If the fixture tests fail, confirm the folder evals/recorded exists with the expected case and portfolio folders.
